title: [Feature/Audio]: Wavetable Morphing Waterfall Spectrum Instrument with LFO Frame Sweeper
body:
## Problem
Wavetable synthesis allows dynamic continuous morphing between vastly different harmonic timbres (from pure sine to woody triangle, buzzing sawtooth, and glassy metallic spectra) using interpolated Fourier tables, which ArcadeVerse's audio tools currently lack.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/wavetable-synth.css`:
   - Synthesizer console with Wavetable Position slider (`0%`–`100%`), LFO Morph Depth & Rate dials, Table Bank selector (`Classic Analog`, `Metallic FM-Like`, `Hollow Vocal`), live single-cycle waveform + waterfall spectrum canvas, and playable 1-octave keyboard.
2. Create modular wavetable engine `assets/js/wavetable-synth.js`:
   - Precompute multi-frame harmonic real/imag Fourier banks and linearly interpolate coefficients dynamically across `PeriodicWave` keyframes without audio clicks.
   - Modulate wavetable position smoothly with an optional LFO sweep and polyphonic ADSR voice envelope management.
3. Pure Vanilla JS/Web Audio API, zero external audio libraries, zero emojis.
4. Add automated test `scripts/test-wavetable-synth.js` validating coefficient linear interpolation, `PeriodicWave` normalization safety, and multi-bank frame indexing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Sweeping the Wavetable Position slider morphs audio timbre and live waveform canvas smoothly.
- [ ] Playable keyboard triggers clean polyphonic voices with ADSR envelopes and zero clicks.
- [ ] Runs gracefully without crashing in headless test environments.
- [ ] Test script `scripts/test-wavetable-synth.js` passes under `node`.
- [ ] Protected core files remain untouched.

title: [Feature/Audio]: Procedural Web Audio Markov Chain Melody Composer with Transition Matrix
body:
## Problem
Procedural game background music often relies on Markov chains to compose infinitely non-repetitive yet musically coherent melodies based on transition probabilities between scale degrees, a concept not yet showcased in ArcadeVerse.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/markov-melody-composer.css`:
   - Interactive composer studio showing a live color-coded `8x8` Markov Transition Probability Matrix heatmap, Scale selector (`Minor Pentatonic`, `Dorian`, `Mixolydian`, `Blues`), Tempo slider, Step Chance slider, and `"Mutate / Reset Matrix"` actions.
2. Create modular algorithmic engine `assets/js/markov-melody-composer.js`:
   - Implement row-normalized Markov transition matrix sampling next note degree deterministically/probabilistically based on previous note state.
   - Allow users to click heatmap cells to bias transitions live and play generated melodies through a clean Web Audio lookahead scheduler (`context.currentTime`).
3. Pure Vanilla JS/Web Audio API, zero external libraries, zero emojis.
4. Add unit test `scripts/test-markov-melody-composer.js` validating probability row normalization, cumulative distribution sampling, and zero-row fallback recovery.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Markov engine generates continuous musical phrases honoring scale intervals and live transition weights.
- [ ] Clicking matrix cells dynamically updates probabilities and highlights the active note transition.
- [ ] Web Audio lookahead clock keeps rhythm steady across tempo adjustments.
- [ ] Standalone test `scripts/test-markov-melody-composer.js` passes under `node`.
- [ ] Protected files remain untouched.

title: [Feature/VFX]: Interactive 2D Physarum Slime Mold Chemotaxis Transport Network Canvas
body:
## Problem
Physarum polycephalum slime mold simulations create astonishing organic vascular networks through thousands of simple pheromone-sensing agents, providing one of the most visually captivating biological algorithms absent from ArcadeVerse.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/physarum-slime.css`:
   - Bioluminescent canvas viewport with controls for Agent Count (`1,000`–`8,000`), Sensor Angle, Sensor Distance, Turn Speed, Trail Evaporation Decay, and Preset Morphologies (`Vascular Web`, `Cellular Rings`, `Filament Tendrils`).
2. Create modular multi-agent simulation `assets/js/physarum-slime.js`:
   - Maintain flat `Float32Array` agent arrays (`x`, `y`, `angle`) and scalar trail buffer (`Float32Array`) with 3x3 box blur diffusion + exponential decay each frame.
   - Implement 3-sensor chemotaxis steering (`left`, `center`, `right` trail sampling) and direct `ImageData` color palette mapping (`Bioluminescent Cyan`, `Amber Spore`, `Neon Violet`).
   - Support mouse click/drag pheromone trail painting or repulsion.
3. Pure Vanilla JS/Canvas `ImageData`, zero external packages, zero emojis.
4. Add automated test `scripts/test-physarum-slime.js` verifying 3-sensor steering direction choice, diffusion energy conservation before decay, and periodic boundary wrapping.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Thousands of slime mold agents self-organize into glowing organic transport networks at interactive framerates.
- [ ] Adjusting sensor angle and distance morphs network topology cleanly between rings, webs, and tendrils.
- [ ] Cursor interaction attracts or paints trails dynamically.
- [ ] Test script `scripts/test-physarum-slime.js` passes under `node`.
- [ ] Protected files remain untouched.

title: [Feature/VFX]: Procedural 2D Animated Truchet Arcs & Geometric Weaving Pattern Canvas
body:
## Problem
Truchet tiles—simple square tiles decorated with asymmetric quarter-circle arcs or diagonal weaves—generate intricate continuous labyrinthine murals and kinetic optical illusions when rotated algorithmically.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/truchet-tiles.css`:
   - Clean geometric canvas studio with controls for Tile Variant (`Quarter Arcs`, `Multi-Scale Recursive`, `Diagonal Maze`, `Cross-Over Weave`), Grid Resolution, Animation Wave (`Radial Ripple`, `Random Flip`, `Static`), Palette selector, and `"Export SVG"` button.
2. Create modular pattern generator `assets/js/truchet-tiles.js`:
   - Compute deterministic/seeded tile orientations and smooth easing angle interpolations (`0 -> 90 deg`) synchronized to spatial wave functions.
   - Render crisp anti-aliased paths on 2D Canvas and serialize identical geometry into standalone downloadable SVG markup.
3. Pure Vanilla JS/Canvas/SVG, zero external libraries, zero emojis.
4. Add unit test `scripts/test-truchet-tiles.js` validating seeded grid reproducibility, orientation modulo states (`0..3`), and valid SVG export generation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Truchet tiles render seamless continuous geometric murals across multiple variants and scales.
- [ ] Wave animation smoothly rotates tiles without tearing or flickering.
- [ ] Exported SVG file accurately reproduces the current pattern state.
- [ ] Unit test `scripts/test-truchet-tiles.js` passes under `node`.
- [ ] Protected core files remain untouched.

title: [Feature/Tools]: Interactive SVG Bezier Path & Snap-Grid Vector Icon Workbench
body:
## Problem
Game creators and UI contributors designing sharp custom SVG icons or geometric badges for ArcadeVerse currently rely on external vector editors instead of an integrated lightweight Bezier path workbench.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/svg-bezier-workbench.css`:
   - Interactive `24x24` / `32x32` snap-grid SVG editor canvas showing anchor nodes, cubic Bezier control handles (`C` / `M` / `Z`), live `1:1` icon preview, Stroke/Fill toggles, and live copyable `<svg>` code output.
2. Create modular vector editor `assets/js/svg-bezier-workbench.js`:
   - Support adding anchor points, dragging cubic control handles with optional grid snapping, closing paths (`Z`), Undo/Redo history, and clearing.
   - Generate clean, minimal formatted SVG `<path d="...">` strings sanitized against invalid numbers.
3. Pure Vanilla JS/Inline SVG DOM, zero external packages, zero emojis.
4. Add unit test `scripts/test-svg-bezier-workbench.js` verifying path `d` serialization (`M`, `C`, `Z`), grid-snap coordinate rounding, and undo/redo stack correctness.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Users can place anchor points, drag cubic Bezier handles, and snap cleanly to grid coordinates.
- [ ] Live `1:1` preview and valid copyable `<svg>` code update instantaneously on every edit.
- [ ] Undo/Redo reliably restores previous path states.
- [ ] Unit test `scripts/test-svg-bezier-workbench.js` passes under `node`.
- [ ] Protected files remain untouched.

title: [Feature/Tools]: Interactive CSS Cubic-Bezier Easing Curve & Keyframe Animation Lab
body:
## Problem
Tuning smooth arcade UI transitions and bouncy animation curves requires guessing numeric `cubic-bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2)` values blindly without visual timing feedback or side-by-side comparison.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/cubic-bezier-lab.css`:
   - Interactive square Bezier curve canvas with draggable `P1`/`P2` handles (supporting overshoot `y < 0` or `y > 1` bounce curves), preset pills (`Ease-Out Back`, `Snap Arcade`, `Smooth Elastic`), live animated comparison race track (`Custom` vs `Linear`), Duration slider, and copyable CSS snippet.
2. Create modular math & preview controller `assets/js/cubic-bezier-lab.js`:
   - Implement exact Newton-Raphson / binary-subdivision cubic Bezier solver `evaluateCubicBezier(x1, y1, x2, y2, t)` for time-accurate custom JS preview racing alongside CSS transitions.
   - Clamp `x1, x2` strictly to `[0, 1]` per CSS Transitions specification while permitting `y1, y2` overshoot `[-0.5, 1.5]`.
3. Pure Vanilla JS/Canvas/CSS3, zero external libraries, zero emojis.
4. Add unit test `scripts/test-cubic-bezier-lab.js` validating endpoint constraints (`f(0)=0`, `f(1)=1`), linear equivalence (`(0,0,1,1)`), `x` clamping `[0,1]`, and CSS output formatting.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Dragging `P1` and `P2` handles updates the Bezier curve, overshoot bounds, and CSS output live.
- [ ] Clicking `"Replay Race"` animates custom vs linear timing strips accurately side by side.
- [ ] `x` coordinates stay strictly clamped within `[0, 1]` so generated CSS is always spec-valid.
- [ ] Standalone test `scripts/test-cubic-bezier-lab.js` passes under `node`.
- [ ] Zero edits to protected files.

title: [Feature/Tools]: In-Browser Retro Hardware Palette Quantizer & WCAG Contrast Matrix Tool
body:
## Problem
Contributors crafting retro pixel themes or game sprites need an offline tool to quantize arbitrary RGB hex colors into authentic 8-bit/16-bit hardware palettes (PICO-8, NES, Game Boy, CGA) and verify WCAG AA/AAA text contrast pairs immediately.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/palette-quantizer.css`:
   - Workbench layout with Palette Selector (`PICO-8`, `Game Boy DMG`, `NES 54`, `CGA`), Sample/Uploaded Image quantized pixel canvas preview, input RGB/Hex nearest-color matcher, and interactive WCAG `NxN` Contrast Matrix grid (`AA`, `AAA`, `Fail` badges).
2. Create modular color-math utility `assets/js/palette-quantizer.js`:
   - Implement nearest-color Euclidean / perceptual weighted RGB distance matcher mapping any pixel or hex color cleanly to the chosen hardware palette.
   - Implement W3C WCAG 2.1 relative luminance `L` and contrast ratio `(L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05)` calculator with zero external color libraries.
3. Pure Vanilla JS/Canvas `ImageData`, zero dependencies, zero emojis.
4. Add unit test `scripts/test-palette-quantizer.js` validating exact WCAG ratios (`#000000` vs `#FFFFFF` == `21.0`), relative luminance math, and nearest palette matching.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Quantizer maps arbitrary hex colors and canvas images accurately onto classic hardware palettes.
- [ ] Contrast matrix computes exact WCAG 2.1 ratios and AA/AAA pass indicators for every foreground/background pair.
- [ ] Works 100% offline with built-in procedural test patterns and optional local image upload.
- [ ] Unit test `scripts/test-palette-quantizer.js` passes under `node`.
- [ ] Protected files remain untouched.

title: [Feature/Physics]: Interactive 2D Newtons Cradle & Elastic Collision Momentum Transfer Physics Lab
body:
## Problem
Demonstrating conservation of linear momentum and kinetic energy through an interactive Newton's Cradle and variable-mass multi-pendulum chain offers a clean tactile physics showcase currently missing from ArcadeVerse.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/newtons-cradle.css`:
   - Clean laboratory canvas frame with controls for Pendulum Count (`3`–`7`), Coefficient of Restitution (`0.5`–`1.0`), Ball Mass Ratio presets (`Equal`, `Heavy Center`, `Graduated`), Gravity slider, and Reset/Release buttons.
2. Create modular physics engine `assets/js/newtons-cradle.js`:
   - Simulate angular pendulum dynamics using RK4/sub-stepped integration for crisp energy stability.
   - Resolve sequential pairwise elastic/inelastic sphere collisions in exact impulse order (`v1'`, `v2'`) with configurable restitution `e` so lifting 1, 2, or 3 balls transfers clean impulse waves across the chain.
   - Support interactive mouse click-and-drag pullback of any pendulum bob and optional Web Audio subtle metallic click clack on impact.
3. Pure Vanilla JS/2D Canvas/Web Audio API, zero external physics engines, zero emojis.
4. Add unit test `scripts/test-newtons-cradle.js` verifying exact elastic equal-mass velocity swap, momentum conservation $\sum m_i v_i$, and sub-unity restitution energy decay.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Pulling and releasing 1, 2, or 3 pendulum spheres cleanly transfers impulses across the resting chain.
- [ ] Variable mass and restitution sliders noticeably alter bounce and momentum transfer physics.
- [ ] High-restitution swings stay stable without runaway energy gain or ball overlap.
- [ ] Standalone test `scripts/test-newtons-cradle.js` passes under `node`.
- [ ] Protected files remain untouched.

title: [Feature/Graphics]: Procedural Hilbert, Peano and Gosper Space-Filling Curve Animator
body:
## Problem
Space-filling fractal curves (Hilbert, Peano, and Gosper flowsnake) continuously map a 1D line across every cell of a 2D grid without ever crossing themselves, creating an iconic algorithmic animation missing from ArcadeVerse.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/space-filling-curves.css`:
   - Canvas viewport with controls for Curve Family (`Hilbert`, `Peano`, `Moore`, `Gosper Flowsnake`), Recursion Order (`1`–`6` safely capped per family), Drawing Speed, Color Mode (`Progress Rainbow`, `Neon Cyan`, `Phosphor Green`), and Play/Pause/Replay buttons.
2. Create modular curve generator `assets/js/space-filling-curves.js`:
   - Generate exact ordered 2D point arrays `[ {x, y}, ... ]` via recursive/iterative index-to-XY algorithms (e.g. Hilbert bit-manipulation `d2xy` or deterministic recursive generators) with strict vertex count bounds preventing memory stalls.
   - Animate progressive polyline drawing along normalized path length with smooth gradient coloring.
3. Pure Vanilla JS/2D Canvas, zero external dependencies, zero emojis.
4. Add automated test `scripts/test-space-filling-curves.js` validating exact vertex counts (`4^n` for Hilbert order `n`, `9^n` for Peano), unit-step adjacency between consecutive points, and zero self-intersections.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Hilbert, Peano, Moore, and Gosper curves animate smoothly along their full continuous paths.
- [ ] Recursion order caps safely prevent browser freezes on deep orders.
- [ ] Color gradient traces progress cleanly from start vertex to end vertex.
- [ ] Test script `scripts/test-space-filling-curves.js` passes under `node`.
- [ ] Protected core files remain untouched.

title: [Feature/Audio]: Interactive Web Audio Shepard Tone & Perpetual Pitch Illusion Synthesizer
body:
## Problem
The Shepard Tone (and Risset Glissando) is a famous auditory illusion used in arcade tension loops and cinema where overlapping octave-spaced sine partials appear to rise or descend endlessly in pitch forever, an audio phenomenon not yet built in ArcadeVerse.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/shepard-tone.css`:
   - Laboratory interface with Direction toggle (`Ascending`, `Descending`, `Paused`), Sweep Speed slider, Octave Voice Count (`4`–`10`), Base Center Frequency slider, Master Volume, and a live spectral bell-curve + gliding partial canvas visualizer.
2. Create modular audio illusion engine `assets/js/shepard-tone.js`:
   - Drive `N` continuous `OscillatorNode` partials spaced cleanly in log-frequency octaves (`f_i = f_min * 2^(phase_i * span)`), wrapping seamlessly at octave boundaries.
   - Weight each oscillator's `GainNode` by a smooth Gaussian bell envelope centered in log-frequency space so boundary wrap-arounds happen at near-zero amplitude with zero audible clicks.
   - Render real-time Gaussian bell envelope and moving octave dots on a 2D Canvas synced to audio phase.
3. Pure Vanilla JS/Web Audio API/Canvas, zero external libraries, zero emojis.
4. Add unit test `scripts/test-shepard-tone.js` validating Gaussian bell gain symmetry, seamless phase wrap-around `[0, 1)`, and total RMS/gain normalization bounds preventing clipping.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Overlapping octave partials create a convincing continuous endless ascending or descending pitch illusion without boundary clicks.
- [ ] Live spectral bell canvas accurately tracks every active partial's frequency and gain amplitude.
- [ ] Audio cleanly pauses, reverses direction, and cleans up oscillator nodes on stop/close.
- [ ] Standalone test `scripts/test-shepard-tone.js` passes under `node`.
- [ ] Protected files remain untouched.
